clue.text: Stretches of water joined by sewers

parts.note: a sea is a large stretch of salt water
the Med is short for the Mediterranean, another stretch of water

explanation.surface: Bodies of water somehow stitched together by drains carrying sewage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewers' looks like drains, but here it means people who sew, so 'joined by sewers' is stitched together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seamed has been stitched along a line, as needlework done by people who sew.

clue.text: Only attractive people get a load of sweets

parts.note: get a load of means look at, and to eye is to look at
candy is sweets

explanation.surface: Only good-looking people are given a pile of confectionery.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye candy is slang for people or things that are visually attractive but not substantial.

clue.text: Peak that's clear, one near borders

indicators.note: borders means the near word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: near in the sense of stingy is mean
to clear is to rid
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mountain top with a view, standing near a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near' looks like close by, but it is the British sense stingy, giving MEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The meridian is the highest point, the peak, as the sun at noon.

clue.text: A do, say, few recollected in Jewish festivals

indicators.note: recollected suggests the letters are gathered together again in a new order

explanation.surface: A party and some remarks remembered from Jewish holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: The Days of Awe are the ten days from Rosh Hashanah to Yom Kippur.
explanation.definitionFit: The Days of Awe are the High Holy Days of the Jewish year.

clue.text: Call Head of Justice, say, a vain sort

parts.note: to call on someone is to pop in for a visit

indicators.note: say tells us to take the letter by how it is spoken, the name of the letter
head of picks out the opening letter of the word Justice

parts.note: the first letter of Justice is J

explanation.surface: An instruction to summon a senior judge, described as conceited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns the letter J into its spoken name, spelt JAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A popinjay is an old word for a vain, foppish person who struts like a parrot.

clue.text: A rant associated originally with an imperial legislator

indicators.note: associated originally suggests the letters are put together in an original, new way

explanation.surface: An outburst connected first of all with an empire's lawmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentarian is a member of a parliament, a lawmaker.

clue.text: Popular performer once seen in woolly

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
ex means former, once
an act is a performer or turn on a bill

explanation.surface: A well-liked former entertainer is seen wearing wool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woolly' looks like knitwear, but it means vague.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolly thinking is vague and imprecise, lacking exactness.

clue.text: Boats going on short trip? Nothing new in this

parts.note: junks are Chinese sailing boats
a hop is a short journey

explanation.surface: Boats going on a brief voyage, with nothing new to report.
explanation.definitionFit: A junk shop sells second-hand goods, so nothing in it is new.

clue.text: Present time eruditely written about? Not right

indicators.note: written about suggests the letters of the word are moved around
not right means the R, for right, is removed

explanation.surface: A Christmas season described learnedly, but wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not right' removes R from ERUDITELY, and 'written about' shuffles the remaining EUDITELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuletide is Christmastime, the season of presents.

clue.text: Shopper wanting booze clutched carrier

indicators.note: clutched means the drink word holds the carrier inside it

parts.note: beer is booze
a tray is something used to carry things

explanation.surface: A customer craving alcohol grabs a carrier bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shopper' is slang for an informer, someone who shops (betrays) another to the police, not a customer.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to shop someone is to inform on them, so a shopper is a traitor or informer.

clue.text: Navy invested in ship part -— it's essential

indicators.note: invested in means the navy abbreviation is placed within the ship part

parts.note: the keel is the bottom structural part of a ship
RN is the abbreviation for the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Naval money is put into a component of a vessel, which is vital.
explanation.definitionFit: The kernel of something is its core, the essential part of it.

clue.text: Not radio broadcast relating to cooking style

indicators.note: broadcast suggests the letters of not radio are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Something not on the wireless is about how food is cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandoori describes food cooked in a tandoor, a clay oven, so it relates to a cooking style.

clue.text: Dog's lead taken from boy by girl on way back

indicators.note: lead taken from means the first letter of boy is used
on way back means the girl's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Tessa is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A dog's leash has been taken off a lad by a girl coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog's lead' reads as a leash, but 'Dog' is the definition and 'lead taken from boy' gives B; 'on way back' turns TESSA into ASSET.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset is a short-legged breed of hound with long ears.

clue.text: I magnify dangers in international armistice

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words international armistice

explanation.surface: A speaker admits to exaggerating the risks of a truce between nations.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarmist is someone who exaggerates dangers, so could say they magnify threats.

clue.text: Most important to overcome doubt in big match

indicators.note: in a down clue overcome means one piece sits over and around another

parts.note: seminal means highly important and influential
an if is a doubt, as in ifs and buts

explanation.surface: Uncertainty must be overcome in a crucial game.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-final is a big match deciding who goes through to the final.

clue.text: Song from that bloke on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means a word is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: that bloke is him

explanation.surface: A song coming from some man being broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn is a religious song of praise.

clue.text: Offence from soccer game in court

definitions.meaning: in football a player other than the goalkeeper touching the ball with a hand commits a foul
a sport where a ball is struck with the hand against walls of a court

explanation.definitionFit: Handball is both a football foul and a court game played with the hands.

clue.text: Unfinished note has upset one born a privileged woman

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the note is dropped

parts.note: a memo is a note

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word has is turned upside down

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A brief note has upset someone born into privilege.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns HAS into SAH. A memsahib was a married European woman in colonial India.
explanation.definitionFit: A memsahib was a respectful title for a European woman of standing in colonial India.

clue.text: Primate coming across saint in church recess

indicators.note: coming across means the primate word spans the saint abbreviation

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey crosses paths with a holy figure in an alcove of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess at the end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Charlie swallowing cream egg and mineral

indicators.note: swallowing means the fool word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a charlie is British slang for a fool, an ass
the cream is the best
O looks like an egg

explanation.surface: A Charlie gulping down a cream egg and a mineral water.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is British slang for a fool; a Cadbury Creme Egg is a popular Easter sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous silicate mineral.

clue.text: Singular person amusing a pedant

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a tickler is one who tickles, amuses

explanation.surface: An odd person entertains a fussy type.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on exactness, which is what a pedant does.

clue.text: Twain and Carroll, say, sign autographs?

definitions.meaning: Mark Twain and Lewis Carroll are both pseudonyms that authors wrote under

explanation.surface: Two famous authors signing their names for fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers' pseudonyms are pen names, and writing signatures is penning names.

clue.text: In gym I'm surprised to fall quickly!

indicators.note: in means the exclamation goes inside the gym abbreviation

parts.note: PT is physical training, gym class
lumme is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone at the gym is shocked to drop suddenly.
explanation.walkthrough: LUMME (also lummy) is an old British cry of surprise, a contraction of 'Lord love me'; PT is physical training, school gym.
explanation.definitionFit: To plummet is to drop straight down fast.

clue.text: Row of rejected places, unmodernised, empty

indicators.note: rejected means the whole string is turned back to front

parts.note: to place is to put, so places is puts

indicators.note: empty means only the outer letters of unmodernised are kept

explanation.surface: A row of discarded, old-fashioned, vacant premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns PUTS plus UD (the outside of 'unmodernised') into DUSTUP; 'Row' is a quarrel, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust-up is a fight or quarrel, which is a row in British usage.

clue.text: Ridiculously close? Far out

indicators.note: ridiculously suggests the letters of close and far are messed up

explanation.surface: Someone complains that something is absurdly near, then far away.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco means in the open air, so eating out of doors is eating out.

clue.text: Party sounded endless

indicators.note: endless means the first and last letters of the word are removed

parts.note: to sound water is to measure its depth, to fathom it

explanation.surface: A party made a noise that never stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounded' seems to mean made a noise; it is measured depth, FATHOMED, which 'endless' trims.
explanation.definitionFit: An at-home is a party or reception held in one's own house.

clue.text: See location for pub instinctively

parts.note: an inn is a pub
at gives a location, so the pub is placed at the see
Ely is a cathedral city and the seat of a bishop, a see

explanation.surface: Look at where a pub is, guided by gut feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not look: it is a bishop's seat, here Ely, an English cathedral city; the phrase reads 'inn at Ely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something innately means doing it by nature, from instinct.

clue.text: Politician gets allowance (without resistance) for drink

parts.note: Lib is short for a Liberal politician

indicators.note: without means the resistance letter is taken out of the allowance word

parts.note: a ration is an allowance
R is the symbol for resistance in physics

explanation.surface: A politician receives expenses, minus any opposition, to spend on drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A libation is a drink, originally one poured out as an offering to a god.

clue.text: Couples from both sides of NI rejected distinction

indicators.note: rejected means each of those end pairs is turned the other way round
couples from both sides of points to the letter pair at each end of the word

parts.note: NI, Northern Ireland, is also called Ulster

explanation.surface: Pairs from both communities in Northern Ireland turned down an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The pairs at each end, UL and ER, are each turned round to LU and RE ('rejected'), leaving ST in the middle. Ulster is the historic province covering Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre means glory or distinction, as well as shine.
